Lakers Nation > Blog > Lakers News > Erik Spoelstra & Bam Adebayo Discuss Challenge Of Guarding Luka Doncic Lakers News Erik Spoelstra & Bam Adebayo Discuss Challenge Of Guarding Luka Doncic
 Ron Gutterman Published: 11/02/2026 4 Min Read Mar 19, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) shoots over Miami Heat center Bam Adebayo (13) during the first half at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Isabella Frias-Imagn Images SHARE The Los Angeles Lakers find themselves in a similar spot as March of last season. Last March, Luka Doncic scored 40 points in a big win over the Houston Rockets on the first night of a back-to-back. On Sunday, Doncic scored 45 in a big win over the Toronto Raptors on the first night of a back-to-back. The Lakers star followed that up, in March, with 60 points against the Miami Heat the very next night. The Lakers play the Heat on Monday night in the exact same context. 
 Hopefully, this means Doncic is in store for another big night, especially given the way he’s been playing this season. He’s averaging an obscene 37.7 points per game, over eight points more than the next-highest scorer (Tyrese Maxey, 29.6). That puts some extra pressure on the Heat and head coach Erik Spoelstra, who have greatly underachieved defensively so far this season (26th in defensive rating). Spoelstra discussed Doncic and Miami’s mindset heading into the game.
 “We’ll find out. He creates a defense and a pick-and-roll coverage all to himself,” Spoelstra said of Doncic this week . “It has to be so unique because of his talents. There’s nothing he hasn’t seen in this league, and he manages every coverage brilliantly. 
 “But I think for us, the more disruptive, the more aggressive we are as a basketball team, just take out who we’re playing against. That has to become our identity, and it has to be more consistent.”
 Bam Adebayo, Miami’s co-star for Giannis Antetokounmpo, also gave an insight into how the Heat want to guard the Lakers star, and it’s similar to what many teams have said in the past. 
 “We’re just going to try and make him make difficult shots. Guys do that in this league. So, for us, it’s making him see double, making him think a little bit, and like I said, try to make guys miss.” 
 Nobody in the NBA is attempting — and making — more 3s per game than Doncic, so this is already the league-wide game plan. However, Doncic is shooting 43.2% from beyond the arc, a number that teams are either going to adjust to, or hope he simply cools off. The Heat seem to be leaning into the latter with Adebayo’s remarks. 
 Doncic has put on a show each and every night so far this season, so there’s no reason to think Monday night will be any different. 
 Luka Doncic makes history on Sunday night
 In L.A.’s win over the Raptors, Doncic became the first player in NBA history to record 15 or more rebounds, five or more steals, five or more assists and five or more 3-pointers in a single game, while also dropping 45 points.
